question: is the media of the artery thinned under the most advanced plaque?
reply:
Based on the provided histological image, **yes**, the media of the artery is thinned under the most advanced part of the plaque.

In advanced atherosclerosis, as the plaque (the large, yellowish, lipid-rich area in the intima) grows, it can compress the underlying tunica media. Additionally, inflammatory processes associated with the plaque can lead to atrophy of the smooth muscle cells in the media, resulting in a noticeable thinning of this layer compared to the relatively unaffected areas of the vessel wall (such as the area on the right side of the image).
